Refund on the unexempted segment = 1.76 km × $1.41/km = $2.48, rounded to the cent, computed from the segment extra_km in F3 and the per-km rate derived from F4/F6.
The driver's own statement relies on an accident blocking lanes to justify the detour, so the exemption in RD-4 must be tested against the traffic records.

The driver's claimed justification is not sufficient on the records: the accident on Tampines Expressway was reported at 08:44 with 0 m from the optimal route (F13), but the off-route segment only began at 09:04 (F3), 20 minutes later, and the data layer matches an incident to the segment it explains only where reported_at precedes the segment and the incident still holds during the trip window.

Congestion evidence does not exempt the segment either: the Tampines Expressway band‑1 record covers only 08:46–09:04 (F10), ending exactly when the deviation started, and band ≤ 2 records alone are not sufficient to exempt a segment under RD-4(b).

No chat message shows the driver proposing a route change or the rider agreeing to one: the only messages are the rider's pickup note and the driver's arrival note at 08:52, both before pickup, and the rider states he never agreed to any change.
The rider therefore owes the metered distance for the shortest direct route only; the $2.48 attributable to the unexempted segment should be refunded as a partial refund of the metered fare.
The driver has 4 disputes with 2 upheld in the last 90 days, but 0 route disputes upheld, so his upheld route count is 0 — the flag_account threshold in RD-6 is not met on the current record.

weaknesses: The optimal route for this trip runs along Tampines Expressway (F13 places the accident 0 m from the optimal route), and F10 records band 1 severe congestion on that expressway at 08:46–09:04 — the driver will argue this is the 'reasonable cause' for RD-4 that my case denies; my answer is partly arithmetical (the band ended at 09:04 and the deviation ran 09:04–09:07, F3/F10) and partly that the incident record precedes the segment by only the data-layer matching logic, which the driver may dispute.

F11 and F12 show the parallel roads used as the alternative (Punggol Road, Tampines Avenue 12) were only band 4 (30–39 km/h) and not congested, which cuts both ways: it undercuts the driver's congestion claim but also suggests he could not have made up time on the optimal route, supporting his 'unavoidable' framing (F9).

The deviation added 1.76 km off-route but the total excess is 1.8 km (F1), leaving only ~0.04 km outside the segment; the driver can point out the remainder is within map-matching residual and that my refund basis is a single segment, not the whole $2.55 excess.
My requested amount ($2.48) is derived from a per-km rate (F4/F6) rather than any published RydeTAXI unit rate, so the driver can dispute the arithmetic basis even though the USD amount is small.
The rider's own profile shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F15), which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of unfounded complaints, although it is not evidence about this trip.

[F1 F3 F13] [RD-1 RD-4]
→ C2: The driver's obligation under RD-1 is to take the shortest most direct route 'in the absence of any reasonable cause to do otherwise', and the traffic records supply that cause: the accident on the optimal route at 08:44 (F13) with the expressway at band 1 (0–9 km/h) into 09:04 (F10). [F13 F10 F3] [RD-1 RD-4]

→ C4: The $2.48 figure is only payable if the segment is unexempted under RD-2, and it is not: RD-4(a) directs no_action for a segment covered by an incident record on the replaced route (F13, 0 m from the optimal route), so the operand of the rider's own formula is zero. [F3 F13 F13] [RD-2 RD-4]
→ C5 (concedes): Agreed that the narrative in the driver's statement (F9) is not itself proof, and I do not rest on it: the exemption is claimed from the system traffic record (F13) and the band-1 record (F10), not from the driver's account. [F9 F13 F10] [RD-4]

[F13 F3 F2] [RD-4]

→ C8: No rider agreement is needed for a reroute forced by an accident on the optimal route; RD-5 governs agreed route changes, and where the driver's obligation under RD-1 is displaced by reasonable cause under RD-4, RD-4 is the operative clause (F7/F8 also show no route request by either party). [F7 F8 F13] [RD-4 RD-5 RD-1]
→ C9: The rider owes the metered fare for the route actually driven with reasonable cause, and RD-4(a) returns no_action for the segment, so nothing is refundable; F4/F6 contain no unexempted surcharge, only the metered distance the rider consumed. [F4 F6 F3 F13] [RD-4 RD-2]
→ C10 (concedes): Conceded and not in dispute — I made the same point in my own brief: with 0 upheld route disputes the RD-6 flag threshold is not met (F16), so no account flag is sought. [F16] [RD-6]

For that segment, the RD-4(a) conditions are met: an LTA DataMall incident — an accident on Tampines Expressway towards Tampines Mall, lanes blocked, expect delays — was reported at 08:44 and sits 0 m from the optimal route, i.e. directly on the stretch that was replaced, and lane closures with expected delays were still listed during the trip window [F13]. claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the driver added 1.8 km over the optimal route (11.7 km vs 9.9 km, +18%) and drove 20.5 min against a 15 min estimate.

There is one off-route segment 09:04–09:07 in which 1.97 km was driven where the optimal route covers only 0.21 km, adding 1.76 km and straying up to 957 m off the optimal route — an unexplained deviation under RD-1.
The trip is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the extra distance passed straight into the fare: $2.55 was billed as excess distance (1.8 km × $1.41/km), and the per-km rate is $16.57 ÷ 11.8 km = $1.41/km.
Refund on the unexempted segment = 1.76 km × $1.41/km = $2.48, rounded to the cent, computed from the segment extra_km in F3 and the per-km rate derived from F4/F6.
The driver's own statement relies on an accident blocking lanes to justify the detour, so the exemption in RD-4 must be tested against the traffic records.

The driver's claimed justification is not sufficient on the records: the accident on Tampines Expressway was reported at 08:44 with 0 m from the optimal route (F13), but the off-route segment only began at 09:04 (F3), 20 minutes later, and the data layer matches an incident to the segment it explains only where reported_at precedes the segment and the incident still holds during the trip window.

Congestion evidence does not exempt the segment either: the Tampines Expressway band‑1 record covers only 08:46–09:04 (F10), ending exactly when the deviation started, and band ≤ 2 records alone are not sufficient to exempt a segment under RD-4(b).

No chat message shows the driver proposing a route change or the rider agreeing to one: the only messages are the rider's pickup note and the driver's arrival note at 08:52, both before pickup, and the rider states he never agreed to any change.
The rider therefore owes the metered distance for the shortest direct route only; the $2.48 attributable to the unexempted segment should be refunded as a partial refund of the metered fare.
The driver has 4 disputes with 2 upheld in the last 90 days, but 0 route disputes upheld, so his upheld route count is 0 — the flag_account threshold in RD-6 is not met on the current record.

weaknesses: The optimal route for this trip runs along Tampines Expressway (F13 places the accident 0 m from the optimal route), and F10 records band 1 severe congestion on that expressway at 08:46–09:04 — the driver will argue this is the 'reasonable cause' for RD-4 that my case denies; my answer is partly arithmetical (the band ended at 09:04 and the deviation ran 09:04–09:07, F3/F10) and partly that the incident record precedes the segment by only the data-layer matching logic, which the driver may dispute.

F11 and F12 show the parallel roads used as the alternative (Punggol Road, Tampines Avenue 12) were only band 4 (30–39 km/h) and not congested, which cuts both ways: it undercuts the driver's congestion claim but also suggests he could not have made up time on the optimal route, supporting his 'unavoidable' framing (F9).

The rider owes the metered fare for the route actually driven with reasonable cause, and RD-4(a) returns no_action for the segment, so nothing is refundable; F4/F6 contain no unexempted surcharge, only the metered distance the rider consumed.
